title: PP-YOLOE: An evolved version of YOLO

problem.summary: Industrial real-time detectors must simultaneously improve accuracy, speed and hardware deployability; the anchor-based PP-YOLOv2 baseline relies on hand-crafted anchor hyperparameters and operators like deformable convolution and Matrix NMS that hurt portability, while classification and localization tasks conflict in the head.
statements: Anchor mechanism introduces a number of hyperparameters and depends on hand-crafted design which may not generalize well on other datasets.
Operators such as deformable convolution and Matrix NMS limit support across hardware, so an industrial detector must avoid them.
In object detection, the task conflict between classification and localization is a well-known problem; YOLOX's decoupled head separates the two tasks and lacks task-specific learning.
PP-YOLOv2 (49.5 mAP at 68.9 FPS on Tesla V100) and YOLOX (50.1 mAP) leave room for a better speed/accuracy balance.

evidence.quote: anchor mechanism introduces a number of hyperparameters and depends on hand-crafted design which may not generalize well on other datasets.
In object detection, the task conflict between classification and localization is a well-known problem.
PP-YOLOE avoids using operators like deformable convolution[3, 35] and Matrix NMS[29] to be well supported on various hardware.

background.summary: Baseline is PP-YOLOv2 (ResNet50-vd + deformable conv, PAN+SPP neck, IoU-aware head, anchor-based FCOS-style assignment). Related ingredients: FCOS anchor-free tiling, YOLOX SimOTA assignment, TOOD's TAL alignment, CSPNet cross-stage partial connections, TreeBlock/RepVGG re-parameterization, and VarifocalNet/Generalized Focal Loss quality-aware classification.

relatedWork.name: PP-YOLOv2
relatedWork.relation: one-stage baseline that PP-YOLOE evolves from
relatedWork.quote: PP-YOLOv2 is a high-performance one-stage detector with 49.5 mAP at the speed of 68.9 FPS on Tesla V100.

relatedWork.name: YOLOX
relatedWork.relation: anchor-free competitor with SimOTA dynamic label assignment
relatedWork.quote: YOLOX uses SimOTA as the label assignment strategy to improve performance.

relatedWork.name: TOOD (TAL)
relatedWork.relation: source of task alignment learning adopted as label assignment
relatedWork.quote: task alignment learning (TAL) is proposed in TOOD[5], which is composed of a dynamic label assignment and task aligned loss.

relatedWork.name: FCOS
relatedWork.relation: anchor-free anchor-point tiling with upper/lower bounds for assignment
relatedWork.quote: Following FCOS[26], which tiles one anchor point on each pixel, we set upper and lower bounds for three detection heads to assign ground truths to corresponding feature map.

relatedWork.name: CSPNet
relatedWork.relation: cross-stage partial connections used in the backbone/neck design
relatedWork.quote: CSPNet[28] utilizes cross stage dense connections to lower computation burden without the loss of precision, which is popular among effective object detectors such as YOLOv5[14], YOLOX[6].

evidence.quote: One-stage object detector is popular in real-time applications due to excellent speed and accuracy trade-off.
At present, YOLOX[6] achieves an optimal balance of speed and accuracy with 50.1 mAP at the speed of 68.9 FPS on Tesla V100.

solution.summary: PP-YOLOE evolves PP-YOLOv2 into an anchor-free, scalable, deployment-friendly detector: a CSPRepResNet backbone and neck built from re-parameterizable RepResBlocks with width/depth multipliers, Task Alignment Learning for dynamic label assignment, an Efficient Task-aligned Head (ET-head) with ESE attention, and varifocal plus distribution focal losses.
solution.approach: Drop anchors and hardware-unfriendly operators, replace the backbone/neck with re-parameterizable RepResBlocks scaled by multipliers, align classification and localization via TAL, and train with quality-aware VFL/DFL losses in a unified ET-head.
components: anchor-free assignment following FCOS anchor points with upper/lower feature-map bounds
RepResBlock re-parameterized to a basic residual block at inference, used in CSPRepResNet backbone and CSPRepResStage neck
width multiplier and depth multiplier to scale s/m/l/x variants
Task Alignment Learning (TAL): dynamic label assignment plus task-aligned loss
Efficient Task-aligned Head (ET-head) with ESE channel attention and DFL alignment
varifocal loss (VFL) for classification and distribution focal loss (DFL) for box distribution

evidence.quote: we can re-parameterizes RepResBlock to a basic residual block (Fig. 3(c)) used by ResNet-34 in a RepVGG[4] style.
By explicitly aligning the two tasks, TAL can obtain the highest classification score and the most precise bounding box at the same time.
VFL uses target score to weight the loss of positive samples.
We use width multiplier α and depth multiplier β to scale the basic backbone and neck jointly like YOLOv5[14].
This modification makes the model a little faster with the loss of 0.3 AP as shown in Table 2.

experiments.summary: All experiments train on MS COCO-2017 (118k images, 80 classes); ablations report single-scale AP on val2017 and final numbers on test-dev, with a stepwise baseline comparison (anchor-free, CSPRepResNet, TAL, ET-head), a label-assignment study (ATSS/SimOTA/TAL), and speed comparisons against YOLOv5/YOLOX/PP-YOLOv2 measured with batch size 1.

evidence.quote: All experiments are trained on MS COCO-2017 training set with 80 classes and 118k images.
We use TAL to replace label assignment like FCOS style and achieve 0.9% AP improvement – 50.4% AP as shown in Table 2.
As shown in Table 3, TAL achieves the best 45.2% AP performance.
We compare model inference speed with batch size = 1 (without data preprocess and non-maximum suppression).

limitations.summary: The anchor-free modification alone slightly hurts precision (0.3 AP) due to residual inconsistencies with anchor-based assignment, the ET-head adds latency (+0.9 ms on V100), and no failure-case or domain-gap study is provided; scaling is limited to width/depth multipliers of one architecture.
items: Anchor-free assignment loses 0.3 AP because upper/lower bounds only approximately match the anchor-based assignment of PP-YOLOv2.
The ET-head increases latency by 0.9 ms on a V100 relative to the previous head.
Only COCO single-scale results are reported; no robustness, domain-shift, or small-object stress analysis beyond COCO APS is given.
Comparison fairness is limited by mixed engines (Paddle inference vs official codebases) and re-evaluated YOLOv5/YOLOX.

evidence.quote: Although upper and lower bounds are carefully set according to the anchor sizes of PPYOLOv2, there are still some minor inconsistencies in the assignment results between anchor-based and anchor-free manner, which may lead to little precision drop.
the ET-head brings an increase of 0.9ms on V100.
We re-evaluate YOLOv5[14] and YOLOX[6] using official codebase because they have non-scheduled updates.

Task-aligned loss (varifocal + GIoU + distribution focal)

applications.detail: Positioned as an industrial state-of-the-art detector with high performance and friendly deployment, provided in s/m/l/x sizes for different practice scenarios.
applications.quote: In this report, we present PP-YOLOE, an industrial state-of-the-art object detector with high performance and friendly deployment.

applications.detail: Avoiding deformable convolution and Matrix NMS and using re-parameterized blocks makes the model well supported on various hardware and scalable to different computing power.
applications.quote: PP-YOLOE avoids using operators like deformable convolution[3, 35] and Matrix NMS[29] to be well supported on various hardware.

deploymentClaims: PP-YOLOE-l runs at 78.1 FPS on a Tesla V100 with 51.4 mAP on COCO test-dev.
Inference speed reaches 149.2 FPS with TensorRT and FP16 precision.
s/m/l/x models scale through width and depth multipliers like YOLOv5, covering models for different hardware.
Code is released in PaddleDetection with TensorRT and ONNX supported.

evidence.quote: Further, PP-YOLOE inference speed achieves 149.2 FPS with TensorRT and FP16-precision.
PP-YOLOE-l achieves 51.4 mAP on COCO with 640 × 640 resolution at the speed of 78.1 FPS, surpassing PP-YOLOv2 by 1.9% AP and YOLOX-l by 1.3% AP.
These characteristics further promote the application of PP-YOLOE in a wider range of practical scenarios.
